claim.quote: Here we demonstrate laser cooling of antihydrogen ... we Doppler-cool a sample of magnetically trapped antihydrogen.

key_value_text.quote: We observe a reduction in the median transverse energy by more than an order of magnitude
key_value_text.value: Median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude; 1S–2S line about four times narrower

name: Laser cooling of antihydrogen atoms

significance.quote: We observe a reduction in the median transverse energy by more than an order of magnitude
significance.value: Median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude (no sigma level stated)

summary.plain: ALPHA cooled trapped antihydrogen atoms with laser light for the first time. The typical sideways energy fell by more than a factor of ten, and the 1S–2S line measured on the cooled atoms became about four times narrower.
summary.technical: One-dimensional Doppler cooling on the 1S–2P Lyman-alpha transition of magnetically trapped antihydrogen; median transverse energy reduced by more than an order of magnitude, and the 1S–2S line is about four times narrower than without cooling.

title: Laser cooling of antihydrogen atoms
why_it_matters: The abstract says a colder, denser antihydrogen sample will drastically improve spectroscopic and gravitational studies.
